current_text: The way out of here is cut into the wall stone, ward-lines deep in the face of it. Coin-gold veins the rock, the same gold that runs the courses overhead.
A carved figure crouches against the far wall, knees drawn up and arms folded in, its eyeless face bowed at the floor. It stays exactly as it is for as long as you stand there.
A waist-high plinth in the ruin's own pale stone, two turns of runes cut around it in the hand that cut the ruin's. The lines all run inward and not one of them comes back out.
Quiet, for a moment. I am tracing a line I cannot see. If I lose it I will blame you, and we will both know I am lying.
The bones stand joint by joint and follow a pace behind you.
Old bones, dry and disjointed, lying out in the open on bare flagstone.
You get a hand on the stub and lean out over the gap. Set a rope here — it is too wide to jump and too smooth to climb.
The floor stops dead and starts again a span out, with the dark going down between. No rope goes anywhere from this lip. The line has to be run from the stub of the broken span.
The flagstone drops half an inch under your palm. A catch clicks somewhere back inside the wall, and nothing comes of it.
A narrow slit at knee height, with the mechanism seated behind the stone. Bare fingers will not reach the catch; this one takes a trap kit.
You follow the mechanism back to its catch and wedge it there with a wax-and-wire pick from the kit. The slit goes dark, and the kit is spent doing it.
A narrow slit at knee height, running the length of the wall. Look at it properly first — there is a mechanism behind it to find.

You look properly, and the floor ahead stops matching the floor behind: the grain runs crossways, and the paint edge stops a finger short of the wall. Months of dust lie on everything down here except that patch.
You step wide around the wire. The dust past it is trodden into a track and the track runs both ways; leave the passage until the delve is under way.
[Observe] — Tool marks in every line of it, top to bottom, and not one line that reads as a lock. The face of it says nothing about what the door is for.
Dust lies over it in one unbroken sheet, and the sheet is centuries thick. Leave the dust where it is.

An alcove beside the sealed door, and something standing in it: ward-stone, shoulder-high, cut in the hand that cut the runes. Its shoulders and its knees carry seams, and no statue in this dungeon has those.
Spoil out of the gap, dropped in two heaps: worked stone in one, plain rubble in the other. Chisel marks decide which heap a piece lands in.
Three coils of rope, dry the whole way through and not a frayed strand in the lot.
The ash inside the stone ring is cold all the way through, and has been for days. The fire-pit is filled in level with the ground, and the rope that was here is gone.
Banked low and raked back into a ring. Heat still comes up off the coals when you put a hand over them.
A cookfire the size of two hands, ringed with stones that did not come out of this ruin. The ash beneath it is deeper than one night's burning.
You put both hands on the stone and it does not shift in its cradle. The court noise drops away while you are trying.

Both spirals hold their light and the seam under the plinth gives at a touch. The near plate first, then its far twin: that was the order it took. Ceria says 'Ksmvr. Down. Carefully.' and has the rope off the stake before you have straightened up.

[Detect Magic] — The ward reads as a lock with the guardian's shape cut into it, and the shape still fits: the seal lets go under your hand. Ceria calls up from the gap: 'Do that again and I'm putting you on the ledger.'
The bones knit themselves upright and take a place at your shoulder.
A ribcage and a scatter of long bones, weathered to the grey-white of the ruin stone around them.
A pit at the middle of the stone ring, the ash in it dead to the bottom. Bones banked up against the stones, every one of them opened for the marrow.
Cracked bones in a heap, dry and light in the hand. Most of them Gnoll; one of them a Drake's.
Two of them, down on their knuckles where the tunnel narrows: moon-grey, shouldered like the rock behind them. Their eyes hold on you and the tunnel keeps dropping away past their feet.

The passage opens into a pillared gallery with no far wall in your light. The floor is packed smooth and hollowed along the lines the pacing takes. Far back, eyes pick up the light and are gone before you can count them.
You cleared this snare earlier today. There is nothing left in the rig to take.
You had the wire off its catch once already today. The silt under it is picked over.
The hinge shears off in your hand and the lid comes away with it. Wax-wrapped and still dry under the silt, 6 gold in a roll.
[Firefly] — The tarred rope takes the flame first and the pile goes after it. The nook stands open behind the ash, with the handle of an iron strongbox showing at the back of it.
A market crate, swollen and split at the seams, sitting where the grate overhead dropped it. Silt fills it to the brim and there is nothing under the silt.
Cable-thick silk in black-and-silver bands, stretched wall to wall. Shield Spiders band their silk like that, and this run of it is new.

Two of them where the silk runs thickest, banded carapaces picking up the moss-light. Their forelegs come off the ground and test the air in your direction. Past them the tunnel drops away, and there are more eyes down there than you are going to stand and count.

The floor here has dropped away into a crack with no bottom in sight. Cold air comes up out of it, colder and drier than anything the sewer holds. The lip is raked with claw-scores, all of them running the same way, down.
